# Generated rows in the format of the dcbrain DRAM error dataset

The three files here have the columns of the DRAM error dataset described at
https://github.com/alibaba-edu/dcbrain/tree/master/dramdata (`mcelog`, `inventory`, `trouble_tickets`).
They hold no row of that dataset. Every row is generated by `fixture()` in
`internal/adapter/dcbrain/fixture_test.go` from fixed seeds:

```
go test ./internal/adapter/dcbrain -run TestFixtureIsCurrent -update
```

The test fails when the files differ from what the generator writes.

Why generated rows: the page that distributes the dataset names two licenses, CC BY-SA 4.0 in its text and
CC-BY-SA-NC 4.0 in its license field. Both are share-alike and one forbids commercial use, so no part of the
dataset is copied into this repository, which is licensed under Apache-2.0.

What the nine servers hold:

| Server | Content |
| --- | --- |
| s0001 | one cell that fails on 24 days |
| s0002 | a row fault that grows over 27 days, then a ticket of failure type 1 |
| s0003 | a column fault found by the scrubber |
| s0004 | errors scattered over one bank |
| s0005 | errors over many banks of one rank, a burst of 150 within an hour, then a ticket of failure type 2 |
| s0006 | scattered errors on both DIMMs of one channel (memoryid 4 and 5) |
| s0007 | three single errors on three DIMMs, and a ticket of failure type 0 |
| s0008 | one error logged five times in one second, and errors of type 3 |
| s0099 | a ticket of failure type 3 and no error row |

The times use the calendar of the dataset, including dates that no calendar year has (`0001-02-30`, `0001-04-31`, `0001-06-31`).
